From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA addendum / CVH — counsel notes (internal)

Vivek / Neha — quick read of Alice's annex and their asks. High-level counsel guidance below (we should keep this tight for commercial):

1) Transfers: we can accept SCCs (processor-to-controller/processor addendum) but we should not commit to an open-ended mechanism that requires us to adopt external controller amendments. Propose: accept EU SCCs + a narrow EU Addendum that excludes training of models on customer content.

2) Subprocessors: 30-day notice is OK; push for right to use 'representative sampling' notice method for low-risk infra vendors. Do not accept an absolute prior-approval requirement.

3) Retention: we need to limit audit/log retention to what's operationally necessary. Counter-propose: 24 months for standard logs, 72 months for security/audit logs with carveouts for subpoena/regulated records. If customer needs 7 years, ask for a business justification and a contract-level fee.

4) Security/KMS: confirm we support customer KMS integration for key material in Private deployments; for Hosted, we offer KMS-backed encryption and can commit to HSM-backed key escrow for enterprise contracts. Call out that model inference outputs are ephemeral and not used for training.

5) Liability / indemnity: keep caps and carveouts aligned with our standard enterprise SOW. Avoid broad data processing indemnities tied to downstream model use.

6) Execution: DocuSign is fine. Request countersignature timeline and require that final execution occurs only after SCCs/addendum are agreed in writing.

I'll produce a marked-up PDF of our suggested language and a short cover memo for sales to send as 'round 1 redlines' — aim to push back on the 7-year retention and the pre-approval subprocessor ask.

Attaching counsel notes.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Counsel_Redlines_11NOV2026.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: DPA addendum & EU-US transfer — Redwood round 1 redlines

Alice — thanks for the addendum. Attaching our counsel's round 1 redlines and a short cover note summarizing the key open items so we can keep procurement moving.

TL;DR on our redlines: we accept EU SCCs (processor-focused) with a narrow addendum but cannot accept an unlimited 7-year retention requirement without justification and potential fee. We will provide a subprocessors list and commit to a 30-day notice window for material changes; for low-risk infra vendors we ask for a sampling notification approach. We confirmed we can support enterprise KMS integrations (Private deployments) and HSM-backed key handling for enterprise SOWs.

Next steps proposed:
- Your team reviews our redlines (attached) and returns any counter-redlines within 10 business days.
- If language on transfers is acceptable, we will route the final annex through DocuSign: https://docusign.com/sign/ABCD-1234
- If Clearview requires 7-year retention as a mandatory term, please provide regulatory justification so we can escalate pricing and operational commitments internally.

Attachments: Redwood_Counsel_Redlines_for_CVH_20261112.docx
Drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/CVH-DPA-redlines

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement + counsel to close this out.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
